recipes.name: Passover Matzo Lasagna
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package shredded mozzarella cheese, divided

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Soak matzo sheets in a large bowl of hot water until tender, about 30 seconds; drain.

Combine eggs, cottage cheese, and 1/2 of the mozzarella cheese in a bowl. Pour 1/2 cup of marinara sauce on the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking pan. Place 2 matzo sheets over the sauce, then pour another layer of sauce over matzo. Spread 1/2 of the cheese mixture on top, then another layer of sauce. Continue layering until all the matzo sheets are used, finishing with a layer of sauce. Sprinkle the remaining mozzarella cheese over the top.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is melted and sauce is bubbly, about 30 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Passover Matzo Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: This lasagna made with matzo sheets instead of lasagna noodles, cottage cheese, mozzarella, and marinara sauce is easy to prep for a tasty Passover dish.

review.reviewBody: This was a very good Passover lasagna with some minor modifications:) I browned and seasoned a 1 lb. of turkey meat and added that to two jars of sauce. I also seasoned the cheese mixture with basil, oregano, salt, and pepper. It came out more beautiful than a traditional lasagna. I will definitely be making this for future. Thank you for providing a base recipe!

I made this by making two square pans worth and adding spinach and mushrooms. It was better than great. My hubby hates pasta but loves this. (Who knew????) I skipped softening the matzo in water. It wasn't necessary. YUM

Wow! I have made this every passover for the past five years, and tastes delicious every time. In terms of the mozerella, I use 4 oz. for the cheese mixture, and then use like 7oz to top off the lasagna. I bake it for longer than 40 min, until the cheese begins to harden slightly at the top. It tastes just like lasagna!

Great, simple recipe. I halved the recipe since I only had 9 inch round pans. I cut off the corners of the Matzah to make it fit and used slices from a block of white cheddar cheese since that's what I had on hand. I also just added an egg to a half-used cottage cheese container so I didn't make any dishes!

This is a very basic outline of a lasagne. You must doctor it up to get any flavor. I used half ricotta and half cottage cheese plus added pecorino romano to egg mixture. I also added a fresh parsley and basil. I finished the top with fresh mozzarella and basil leaves. It still didn’t have much flavor. Next time I will add more fresh herbs, crushed red pepper, and kosher salt.

Made this recipe for my chavurah (friends group). I hadn't tried it before, and was wary of how much cottage cheese vs shredded mozzarella. It was fantastic, and everyone loved it!! I need to use 1 1/2 pieced of matzah each level to fit a large casserole dish; this worked perfectly. Also need more marinara sauce, about 1/2 more jar. I will use this recipe forever!!

This is how I make it every year. The one change is, do NOT soak the matza first. Start with a thin layer of sauce, then the one piece of dry matza, continue with the layering (using 1 matza per layer) until you reach the top of your pan. The sauce and other ingredients will moisten the matza perfectly.

I used a 16 oz container of cottage cheese (because that's what I had) and about 12oz of shredded mozzarella) and 3 extra large eggs (because they looked very big).
I also only had a 26oz jar of pasta sauce, so that's what I used, and it was the perfect amount for my 9x13 pan, but I did need about 8 matza boards....

The basic recipe is wonderful, basic and easy to adjust to individual taste.

Great chol hamoed lunch and breakfast.
For those who none-Gebrach, I recommend making for issrue chag or motzei yom tov (instead of waiting in line to buy raw pizza or bagels)
 Pesach matzao is also much "cleaner" then noodles because it's made from clean, unprocessed wheat. 

Wondering dish!

Delicious! I was worried that it wouldn't taste like real lasagna. You couldn't even tell that it was matzo! The matzo tasted just like lasagna noodles! I added basil, broccoli, and mushrooms! I substituted the cottage cheese for ricotta. Add lots of Parmesan! Great recipe!

This turned out great! I loved the cottage cheese and mozzarella combo and was thrilled (and a bit surprised) by how tender the matzo got. As a little bonus, I sauteed some spinach and garlic and added it on top of the cheese layers just to add a little vegetable. It was a hit, not only with my vegetarian seder guest, but with the whole crowd. I will definitely do it again.

I 've made a version of this recipe for well over 20 years. My tweaks would be to not moisten the matzoh as all of the ingredients used will provide sufficient moisture. Instead of cottage cheese I use whole milk ricotta cheese as the full fat of the cheese adds extra texture and improved taste. Finally sometimes I will add a layer of spinach if I want a more vegetable oriented lasagna.
Quick and easy
Very inventive

I made my own marinara sauce, so I felt like there was a lot of flavor. Also, I used the salty gluten free matzah, so there was some good flavor. I made it for my family and they loved it. It was devoured in less than 15 minutes.
Loved it! Thank you! Delicious and easy

I am gluten free and used oat matzo and instead of actual marinara, I used tomato sauce that was just tomatoes, sea salt, onion and garlic. I also used more mozzarella and an additional egg. So, too much cheese, it would have been better to stick to the recipe where that is concerned. And marinara would've been better to, but didn't have anything that was OK for passover in the house. And the oat matzo definitely depends on the brand. The open box didn't have 6 whole sheets so I opened another brand that is thicker. It has a weird taste that didn't work with the lasagna. It's fine if you're covering it with something strong like horseradish, but not tomato sauce. It only added to the tinny taste from the tomato sauce. Not sure, as a gluten free person, that I would try it again.
This is a really good recipe that everyone will eat during Passover
I didn't even realize I was eating matzah! This is good anytime, not just for Passover. Next time, I'll add some chopped spinach :)
I made it with Fat Free Cottage Cheese, Fat Free Mozzerella and Francesco Rinaldi or Barilla Pasta Sauce. I have been making it for several years now. It is DELICIOUS! It tastes just like Lasagna.
Very yummy! The hubby loved it also will def make this again.
